uncited: This method quantifies the geometric and scalar approximation error introduced when an unstructured grid volume is resampled into a Pixel Ray Image (PRI).
It differs from sibling methods like [PRI Texture Storage](2493-pri-texture-storage.md) by focusing on quantitative error analysis rather than data layout optimization.
*   The method operates on the logical representation of the grid $V$ and the reconstructed scalar field from $P$.
No specific binary layout is required for the error calculation itself, as it relies on evaluating vertices.
Iterate over every tetrahedron $t$ in the original grid $V$.
For each tetrahedron $t$, identify its four vertices $v \in t$.
For each vertex $v$, retrieve the original scalar value $S(v)$ from the grid $V$.
Reconstruct the scalar value $S_P(v)$ at the same spatial location using the PRI $P$.
Compute the residual error for the vertex: $|S(v) - S_P(v)|$.
Calculate the volume $|t|$ of the tetrahedron.
9.  (Optional) Use the MSE to compute PSNR if the maximum possible scalar value range is known.
*   Error threshold: In practice, this metric is used to determine simplification thresholds.
*   Precision issues may arise if $S(v)$ and $S_P(v)$ are very close; double precision is recommended for error accumulation.
It is computationally inexpensive relative to the rendering cost but requires random access to the original grid data.
*   **Strengths:** Provides a physically meaningful error metric weighted by volume, accounting for the size of geometric elements.
*   **Limitations:** Requires access to the original unstructured grid $V$ and its vertex data, which may not be available in purely image-based pipelines where only the PRI is retained.
The method was introduced in the context of GPU-based unstructured grid volume rendering using an image-based modeling approach.

Source [S2] confirms the same methodology. Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
